text:
incident-bot: ALERT: high tail latency detected in eu-west-1 (streaming routes). p95 = 420ms (SLO 200ms), p99 = 3.7s (SLO 1s). Streaming stalls and increased decode time starting ~12:03 UTC. KV cache eviction-rate spiked ~12:04 UTC. Triggering on-call notification.
Anika: grabbing dashboards now. I can see a big jump in KV eviction_rate and slab fragmentation on shard 12.
Ravi: ack, joining. Seeing prefill queue backlog + many requests falling back to full decode. Prefill-to-decode ratio went from 0.8 to 0.22.
Jules: support: we already have two customers reporting degraded streaming responses (partial chunks then long pause). Tickets #40021, #40022. Both on eu-west-1.
Marta: I'm taking lead. First priority: stop customer impact. Second: find root cause (eviction/prefill imbalance?).
Anika: quick notes from metrics: top offenders are long-context chat sessions (seq_len>5k) and one hot model variant rdx-chat-14b-quant that has high KV footprint.
Ravi: rolling list of mitigations I can do now: 1) temporarily increase eviction threshold to keep more prefill keys (raise low_watermark), 2) reduce prefill window for streaming routes (disable prefill for streaming for 30m), 3) route a portion of traffic to eu-central fallback pool. Which to prioritize?
Marta: do (2) and (3) now. Eviction threshold change might increase memory pressure. We want immediate reduction in prefill pressure.
Ravi: doing disable prefill for streaming routes:
```bash
# disable prefill flag for streaming route in prod config
curl -X POST https://config.redwood.internal/api/v1/flags -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN' -d '{"flag":"prefill.streaming.enabled","value":false}'
```
Ravi: applied. Confirming via /admin/routes: streaming prefill = false
Anika: I’m starting a short canary reroute 15% -> eu-central fallback pool for rdx-chat-14b-quant: kubectl patch svc routing ...
deploy-bot: Routing change: canary 15% -> eu-central applied by Anika at 12:12 UTC (change-id: r1234).
Ravi: eviction rate decreased slightly but p99 still high. Heap fragmentation still elevated. I'm going to force compact slab on shard 12 (non-disruptive), will run compaction tooling.
Jules: customer updates: told both customers we are actively mitigating, ETA 20-30m. They asked if data loss: no.
Ravi: running compaction:
```text
> /srv/kv-tools/compact --shard=12 --concurrency=2
compaction started, est 6m
```
Anika: after compaction started, p95 improved to 210ms, p99 dropped to ~1.6s. Still above SLO but much better. Streaming stalls count down 40%.
Marta: good. Next: add protection against future single-model hotkeys. Can we add a soft limit on KV prefix size per model?
Ravi: we have a quick knob: per-model prefill_budget. Setting rdx-chat-14b-quant prefill_budget=0.5 (half default) to reduce prefill kv population. Applying now.
Ravi: applied prefill_budget change. Observing traffic: prefill hit-rate down to 0.3, decode request count rose marginally but tail improved.
Anika: I'm going to open a short-lived circuit-breaker for long-context sessions > 8k tokens to avoid compounding the slab fragmentation while we stabilize.
Marta: go ahead. Also schedule a live handoff to eng-sre for deeper follow-up and postmortem.
Jules: support: customers acknowledge improvement, will keep monitoring. I asked for any request logs showing repeated hot prefixes to share.
Ravi: followup checks: KV slab usage before fix: 92% on shard12, after compaction: 68%. Evictions per minute down from 14k to 1.2k.
Anika: p95 back to 185ms (within SLO), p99 ~950ms (just under 1s). Streaming stalls are at 8% of previous peak.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: reduced to P1 -> monitoring. Time to stabilize: 12:31 UTC.
Marta: handoff to eng-sre for full root-cause (likely combination of long-tail sessions + model-specific high-prefix churn + inadequate slab allocation). Eng-sre can take ownership for postmortem.
Anika: assigning to Ravi and team for next 72h follow-up, tracking actions: 1) add per-model prefix caps, 2) improve prefill vs decode heuristics (favor decode if kv pressure high), 3) alert thresholds for slab fragmentation, 4) playbook update for streaming fallback.
Ravi: I'll draft the mitigation runbook changes and put link here once ready.
Marta: thanks everyone. Quick notes for postmortem: customer impact window ~12:03-12:31 UTC, 2 customers with degraded streaming, SLO breached for ~28 minutes, root cause: KV cache pressure + slab fragmentation + prefill/decode imbalance prioritizing prefill.
Jules: adding support ticket IDs to incident: #40021, #40022.
support-bot: Noted. Tickets updated with incident ID INC-2026-175800.
Marta: closing thread to proceed with RCA. If anyone sees re-regression reopen thread. :thumbsup:
